A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Stronger-MAS work and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–H. The appendices match after a one-page pagination shift.

before.justification: v3 reports original benchmark evaluations, agent-scaling experiments, ablations, and latency measurements in Section 5 and Appendices E–G.

after.justification: v5 retains the original empirical results in Section 5 and Appendices E–G, including benchmark scores, ablations, and latency measurements.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, objectives, reward designs, policy-sharing options, and training system are unchanged. The revised arrows in Figure 3(b) illustrate the tree-sampling procedure already specified in v3.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same game, planning, coding, and mathematics coverage, including Sudoku, Sokoban, Plan-Path, APPS, LiveCodeBench, CodeContests, AIME, OlympiadBench, and GSM8K comparisons. Appendix scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 retain the same single-agent, MAS, and GRPO variants and the MAPORL, MARFT, and CURE comparisons. The cited baseline results and appendix comparator sets are unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 and Appendix C retain the same models, datasets and splits, metrics, sampling factor K=4, turn horizon T=4, and 150-step training budget. Supplementary evaluation procedures are also unchanged.

E4.justification: The agent-scaling analysis, isolated-training and policy-swapping ablations, reward and alignment analyses, outcome-only reward experiments, multi-turn single-agent comparisons, latency study, and case studies are all retained without revision.

E5.justification: Figure 6(a) retains the same shaded variability across runs and its caption. Seed disclosures and statistical reporting practices are unchanged; no run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: Numerical and qualitative results match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 2 retains 98.00% Sokoban and 57.00% AIME24 accuracy for Qwen3-8B with per-role policies.

T1.justification: The Markov-game formulation, optimization equations, reward definitions, Appendix B.7 assumption, lemma and proposition with proofs, and Appendix G complexity derivations are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same algorithm and system contributions, performance claims, role-specialization claim, and task-dependent choice between shared and specialized policies.

C2.justification: Interpretations of coordination, specialization, GRPO grouping failures, reward shaping, single-agent refinement, and computational scaling are unchanged. No new applicability boundaries or substantive limitations are introduced.

D1.justification: v5 adds a specific PettingLLMs repository link under 'Code & Environment' after the abstract. v3 only described supplementary code and a future public release in Section 8. Implementation details remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish repository completeness.

R1.justification: Section 2, Appendix A, and the bibliography retain the same cited works and research positioning, including the qualification that the MARFT comparison concerns its v3.

P1.justification: A short 'Code & Environment' block is inserted after the abstract, and the arXiv version/date stamp is updated. Existing prose, terminology, section hierarchy, and appendix organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 3(b) redraws trajectory connections as branching arrows from selected candidates. The added front-page block also reflows text and figure placement, moving the conclusion onto a separate page. Tables and remaining figure content are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v5 makes Figure 3(b) better distinguish tree sampling from parallel trajectories and supplies a direct code/environment repository address. These modest gains in clarity and reproducibility guidance outweigh the minor pagination inefficiency. Scientific evidence is unchanged, and repository completeness cannot be verified from the PDFs.
